verdict.rationale: ClickUp lists "Automations" as a first-party product feature, and its developer site says you can "trigger workflows from ClickUp events." Together these suggest native event-driven automation, but the evidence is only feature labels with no description of how rules are built. Third-party automation through n8n is a user-side workaround and is not credited. missing for 10: documentation of a trigger/condition/action rule builder, the available triggers and actions, any limits or plan restrictions, and independent or hands-on corroboration that rules eliminate manual steps.
